races.title: State House, District 82
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brian Echevarria
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 82, in office since January 2025. Financial advisor, small business owner and building contractor. Former Cabarrus County GOP chairman. Lost re-election on Nov 3, 2026 to Democrat Chris Bishopp.
cands.gaps: We found no bills he sponsored (the sponsored-legislation table on his Ballotpedia page was empty), so there are no documented legislative actions on the platform issues. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or growth, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. His campaign site speaks only in general terms about parental rights, education and constitutional freedoms. We found no endorsements, no controversies and no foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. His 2022 survey does not say where he grew up or his age when he moved to North Carolina. No source confirms his birth year.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served one term in the NC House (2025-2026). Works as a financial advisor, small business owner and building contractor. Former Cabarrus County GOP chairman, a party post rather than an elected office.
qual.why: One term of legislative service plus a finance career and business ownership. The score is held in the middle-to-upper range because the legislative record is a single term, and committee posts such as vice chair are not counted.
qual.label: One term of legislative service plus a finance career and business ownership. The score is held in the middle-to-upper range because the legislative record is a single term, and committee posts such as vice chair are not counted.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says good governments protect residents' homes from unaffordable, unsustainable property tax hikes, and that he works to keep more of residents' money in their homes and focuses on property tax issues.

cands.name: Chris Bishopp
cands.bio: Navy veteran and retired Federal Aviation Administration air traffic controller. He served about seven years as a Navy flight officer and then more than 30 years as a controller, supervisor and quality control specialist. He was the Greensboro tower's legislative representative for the controllers' union. Democrat elected to NC House District 82 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from the Sway voting groups 92% Club, Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Imani's Pix, Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and YALLvote.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Bishopp was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. He has held no prior elected office, so there is no legislative record to review. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or policing. His statements on taxes and growth are general. Reporting on any controversies was not available in the pages reviewed.

qual.background: Naval flight officer for about seven years, then 31 years with the FAA as an air traffic controller, supervisor and quality control specialist. He served several years as legislative representative for the Greensboro tower in the controllers' union (NATCA). He has held no elected office.
qual.why: He has a long career in supervision and public safety and some legislative advocacy experience. He has no prior legislative or elected service and no budget or law career, so he scores in the middle range.
